transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we go any further, I want to make clear where things stand. The solvent-recovery skid is installed beside the coating area, but it has not yet been used on production solvent. We have nine hundred liters of solvent mixture in labeled drums awaiting a disposition decision. I am the one who makes the final authorization decision on whether we proceed with a trial run. Per plant policy, I am required to conduct a pre-job review with process engineering, maintenance, and environmental compliance before I can authorize anything. The standard pre-job procedure requires an equipment inspection, closed transfer, ventilation verification, vapor monitoring, and documented waste handling before solvent recovery begins. I want us to go through each of those requirements today, identify what has been completed and what has not, and assign clear commitments for anything still outstanding. I will not authorize the trial until every requirement is either satisfied or has a concrete commitment assigned and then fulfilled. Let's start by hearing from each of you on the status of your respective areas.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to share something important from my bench compatibility test. I completed the test yesterday, but the result is still only in my lab notebook and hasn't been uploaded to the process file yet. What I found is that only 600 liters of the stored 900-liter mixture is suitable for this skid. The remaining 300 liters contains a solvent component that the skid's seals are not rated for. We'll need to segregate that 300 liters and exclude it from the trial, and I'll get the full report uploaded to the process file as part of my commitments.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I completed the pre-use inspection of the solvent-recovery skid, and I found that the transfer pump seal must be replaced and pressure-tested before we can operate the skid. The good news is that the seal kit is already in the maintenance storeroom, and the replacement takes exactly three hours. However, I should note that I recorded this finding on a paper inspection sheet that has not yet been entered into the electronic work-order system. I'll take on the commitment to replace the seal, pressure-test it, and get the inspection record entered into the electronic system before any trial run proceeds.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share something critical from my permit review. I received clarification from the environmental office this morning. This solvent recovery operation requires ventilation of at least 6 air changes per hour, exactly 2 continuously operating LEL monitors, and a hazardous-waste manifest for the incompatible 300 liters that Jonas just identified. I have not yet filed this permitting clarification with the trial paperwork, so I want it on the table now as we go through the pre-job review. The ventilation rate, the LEL monitor count, and the hazardous-waste manifest for that 300 liters all need to be verified before authorization.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Upload full bench compatibility test report to the process file, including finding that only 600 liters is compatible and 300 liters must be segregated and excluded from the trial.
Physically segregate the 300 liters of incompatible solvent mixture from the 600 liters approved for the trial.
Replace the transfer pump seal using the seal kit from the maintenance storeroom, pressure-test the replacement, and enter the paper inspection record into the electronic work-order system.

File the environmental office permitting clarification with the trial paperwork, including the 6 ACH ventilation requirement, 2 continuous LEL monitor requirement, and hazardous-waste manifest requirement for the 300 liters of incompatible solvent.
Verify that ventilation achieves at least 6 air changes per hour in the coating area before the trial proceeds.
Verify that exactly 2 continuously operating LEL monitors are installed and functional before the trial proceeds.
Complete a hazardous-waste manifest for the 300 liters of incompatible solvent identified by Jonas before the trial proceeds.
Verify closed transfer procedure is established and documented for moving the 600 liters of compatible solvent from drums to the skid.
Verify vapor monitoring protocol is in place and operational in coordination with the 2 continuous LEL monitors.
